cards.subject: An aged Roman bishop of the 380s, half-length, turned a little to the left in three-quarter view, in the dress of his own century and NOT a later papal tiara: a long white tunic, a deep red bell-shaped paenula (chasuble) falling in soft folds, and over it a narrow white woollen pallium marked with small dark crosses hanging down the front; on his head a low, rounded white cap. He holds a thick bound codex of the Scriptures against his breast in his left hand and raises his right hand in a gentle blessing. Behind him the catacomb of San Callisto on the Via Appia, which he adorned for the martyrs: a tufa gallery lit by small clay oil lamps, rows of closed wall-tombs, and the arched opening of the crypt of the popes with two slender marble columns; any marble slab is plain, with no carving. Through an opening at the right, a glimpse of the Appian Way with umbrella pines and cypresses in evening light. Keep the gallery inside the arched window.
cards.face: A Roman of Spanish stock, about seventy-five, with a broad-browed, RECTANGULAR face — a wide, flat forehead, a long straight nose with a broad bridge, large, wide-set dark eyes under level, heavy grey brows, flat broad cheekbones, a strong, square jaw and a firm, straight mouth; short grey hair showing under the cap at the temples; a short, ROUNDED grey-and-white beard trimmed close to the jaw, with a grey moustache; a calm, watchful gaze looking out a little to the side. Not a flowing white-bearded patriarch: the beard is short and round.
cards.basis: No likeness survives; the Lund Gospels miniature (c. 1150) we checked shows him with short grey hair, a short rounded grey beard, a long nose and wide-set eyes, in a red chasuble and a pallium with small crosses under a low white cap. The card keeps those marks and sets him in San Callisto, among the martyrs' tombs he honoured with his inscriptions.

cards.subject: An old Polish priest and master of the Kraków Academy in the 1460s, half-length, turned a little to the right in three-quarter view, bareheaded, in a black academic doctor's gown with wide sleeves and a deep red lining, a white collar at the neck; his black biretta rests on a closed book in the crook of his left arm. With his right hand he lays his own dark wool cloak over the shoulders of a thin, barefoot young student standing small at the lower right, as the story of his charity tells. Behind them the arcaded Gothic courtyard of the Collegium Maius in Kraków — red brick, pale stone arcades, a steep tiled roof — under a light fall of snow on a winter evening, a warm light in the windows. Keep the student and the courtyard inside the arched window.
cards.face: John: an old Pole of about seventy-five with a LONG, NARROW, sculpted face — a very high bald forehead and crown ringed by a short wreath of grey-white hair, prominent high cheekbones, a straight nose, heavy-lidded, half-closed gentle grey eyes, a ruddy complexion, full prominent lips, and a short, close grey beard following the line of the jaw; a kindly, downcast look toward the student. The student: a pale, thin Polish lad of about seventeen with a narrow face, straw-fair hair cut straight across the brow, and wide grateful blue eyes.
cards.basis: The inventory of sacred art of Małopolska describes his old portraits: an elderly balding man with a wreath of grey hair and a short grey beard, a high bald forehead, a ruddy face, a straight nose and full lips; another has an elongated face with half-closed eyes and prominent cheekbones, in a doctor's gown lined with red. The courtyard is the Collegium Maius, where he taught and lived, and the cloak is his best-known charity.

cards.subject: The miraculous image of Nossa Senhora da Conceição Aparecida exactly as venerated in her basilica: a SMALL terracotta statue of the Immaculate Conception with a dark cinnamon-brown face and dark joined hands, clearly a statue and not a living woman, wrapped in her stiff, triangular royal-blue mantle embroidered with gold and edged in gold, which falls from the shoulders to the base, and wearing a jewelled imperial gold crown; no flags, no ribbons with writing. The little image stands radiant in a soft golden glow just above a wooden dugout canoe on the broad, calm Paraíba do Sul river at dawn, the dripping fishing net draped below her and heavy with silver fish. In the canoe, small and half-length, the three fishermen of 1717 kneel and look up at her in awe. Behind them green river banks of Atlantic forest, palms and the blue ridge of the Serra da Mantiqueira under a pink sunrise. Keep the canoe, the net and the river inside the arched window.
cards.face: The image: the statue's own small, dark cinnamon-brown terracotta face — a round, gentle girl's face with lowered eyes and the hint of a smile, framed by the crown and mantle, hands joined at the breast. The fishermen, colonial caboclos of the Paraíba valley with warm brown skin, in coarse white cotton shirts and rolled trousers: Domingos Garcia (left), about fifty, a broad, SQUARE face with heavy cheekbones, a flat wide nose, deep-set eyes and grey stubble, under a frayed straw hat held to his chest; João Alves (centre), about twenty-five, a lean, LONG face with a narrow jaw, straight black hair and a thin black moustache, holding the net; Filipe Pedroso (right), about forty, a full ROUND face with a short black beard and bright dark eyes, hands raised in wonder.
cards.basis: The image itself is the face: a 36 cm terracotta Immaculate Conception darkened to a cinnamon colour by the river and by centuries of candle soot, wearing the blue gold-embroidered mantle and the jewelled crown given by Princess Isabel in 1888. The three fishermen, the Paraíba do Sul, the net that brought up body and head and then the great catch follow the account of 1717.

cards.subject: Saul of Tarsus struck down on the road to Damascus, half-length and close: thrown to the ground on one knee and one hand, his head lifted, his right arm raised to shield his dazzled eyes from a great shaft of white-gold light that pours down from an opening in the clouds at the upper left; he wears a deep red tunic, a blue travelling cloak slipping from his shoulders and a sword at his belt, the persecutor's sword that becomes his emblem. Behind him his startled chestnut horse rears, and two small companions in plain tunics shrink back, seeing the light but no one. Beyond, the stony road runs toward the walled city of Damascus among green orchards, with snow-capped Mount Hermon on the horizon. Keep the horse and the companions inside the arched window.
cards.face: Paul as on the paul card, a little younger (about forty-five): a noble, kindly LONG face — a high domed forehead, bald on top with a receding hairline and dark wavy hair at the sides, a straight fine nose, calm luminous dark eyes now wide with awe, a long dark pointed beard reaching well below the chin. The companions: small, one a young man with a round face and short black hair, the other older with a grey short beard, both faces half-turned away.
cards.basis: Paul keeps the face of the existing paul card (bald crown, dark wavy side hair, long dark pointed beard), the Byzantine type from the Painter's Manual. The scene follows Acts 9:3-7 and the Western tradition of the fall from the horse, as in Caravaggio's Conversion on the Way to Damascus.

cards.subject: St. Peter enthroned as teacher, seated frontally and half-length on an ancient wooden chair with a high back decorated with carved ivory panels, in his blue tunic and golden-ochre mantle as on the peter card; his right hand raised with two fingers extended in teaching, his left hand holding the two great keys, one gold and one silver, and an open codex resting on his knee. Behind and above him the apse of St. Peter's Basilica: the golden glory of rays and clouds around the round amber window of the Holy Spirit with the white dove, warm light falling on the chair; no lettering anywhere. Keep the chair and the glory inside the arched window.
cards.face: Peter as on the peter card: an elderly man around sixty-five with a broad, weathered fisherman's face, a strong wide nose, deep-set earnest eyes and a lined forehead; curly grey-white hair balding from the back of the head with a curly tuft left at the forehead; a short, square, curly grey-white beard; a steady, teaching gaze straight out at the viewer.
cards.basis: Peter keeps the face of the existing peter card, the Byzantine type (short curly grey hair and beard, the forelock). The feast honours his office as teacher; the chair with ivory panels and Bernini's glory in the apse of St. Peter's are its real emblem in Rome.

cards.subject: St. John the Baptist in the dungeon of Machaerus on the night before his death, half-length, seated on a stone ledge in his camel-hair garment and a faded red mantle, his wrists loosely chained; he holds his slender reed cross against his shoulder and lifts his face in prayer toward a shaft of moonlight falling through a small barred window high in the rock wall. Through the bars, the moonlit Dead Sea and the hills of Judaea far below the fortress. In the dark doorway at the right, only the long shadow of a guard and the faint gleam of a sword hilt: his death is implied, never shown. No blood, no charger, no head. Keep the cell inside the arched window.
cards.face: John as on the john_baptist card, made ascetic by prison: a lean man of about thirty with a LONG face — high cheekbones over hollowed cheeks, a straight nose, large dark-brown eyes under straight dark brows, a firm mouth; thick, unkempt curly dark-brown hair to the shoulders and a rough, short dark-brown beard; the gaze lifted to the light, steadfast and at peace. Not a Christ type: wild hair, weathered skin, wilderness gauntness.
cards.basis: John keeps the face of the existing john_baptist card. Josephus names Machaerus, above the Dead Sea, as his prison and place of death; Mark 6:17-29 tells of the imprisonment and the beheading, which the card leaves to the sword implied in the doorway.

cards.subject: The naming of Jesus on the eighth day (Luke 2:21), with nothing of the rite itself shown: in the lamplit room of a simple stone house in Bethlehem, Our Lady sits holding the Infant wrapped in white linen on her lap; an elderly village elder in a white robe with a blue-striped prayer shawl over his head stands beside her and raises his right hand over the Child as he names him; St. Joseph stands behind Mary, bowing his head, a hand on his breast. On a low wooden table a small silver bowl, a folded white cloth and a lit clay lamp; no knife, no instrument. Through an open window, the terraced hills of Bethlehem at dusk with the first star. Half-length figures close together; keep them inside the arched window.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, lids lowered in a recollected gaze, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head. The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md: a plump, ROUND baby face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls, a plain gold halo, a newborn eight days old, eyes open and calm. St. Joseph as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about forty with a LONG OVAL face — a straight nose, gentle dark-brown eyes under level brows, a quiet mouth; full dark-brown curly hair to the nape and a short full dark-brown beard; green tunic and ochre-brown mantle. The elder: about sixty-five, a broad, ROUND face with full cheeks and a short, rounded grey beard, a short wide nose, kind crinkled dark eyes under bushy grey brows — clearly not Simeon's long face.
cards.basis: The scene follows Luke 2:21, which says only that the Child was circumcised and named Jesus on the eighth day; the card paints the naming, in a Bethlehem house, and keeps Our Lady, the Child and Joseph as on the Nativity and Epiphany cards. A book feast of the Pictorial Lives (1 January).

cards.subject: The Child Jesus in glory, adored in heaven and on earth, after the manner of Gaulli's Triumph of the Name of Jesus but without its letters: the Child, about three years old, stands on a bank of clouds in the upper centre within a great golden sunburst of rays that holds NO letters or monogram, wearing a simple white tunic, his right hand raised in blessing and his left holding a small gold globe with a cross. Below him, on either side, two kneeling angels in rose and green robes bow with hands crossed on their breasts; lower still, small and serene, the faithful of every age kneel on a green hillside above Bethlehem, looking up. Keep the clouds, angels and people inside the arched window; no text anywhere.
cards.face: The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md: a plump, ROUND child's face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls, a plain gold halo, now a child of about three with a steady, gentle gaze looking out at the viewer. cards.basis: The feast honours the Name at which every knee bends (Philippians 2:10, its entrance antiphon); the Gesù's ceiling by Gaulli paints heaven and earth adoring the Name in a burst of light. The card keeps that adoration but shows the Child himself, with the Christ Child's face from recurring-figures.md, because the card allows no lettering.

cards.subject: The Presentation in the Temple (Luke 2:22-38), figures half-length and close: at the centre the aged Simeon holds the Infant Jesus in his arms, his hands veiled in a fold of his white mantle, and lifts his eyes to heaven as he sings his canticle; at the left Our Lady, her hands still open toward her Son, and St. Joseph behind her holding a small wicker basket with two white turtledoves; at the right the prophetess Anna, very old, in a dark-blue veil, raising one hand toward the Child and holding a closed scroll. Behind them the Temple of Jerusalem: Herodian colonnades of pale stone, bronze doors, a golden seven-branched lampstand and the rising smoke of incense in warm light. No lettering. Keep all five figures inside the arched window.
cards.face: Our Lady as in recurring-figures.md: a young woman of about eighteen with a delicate, softly OVAL face — a smooth high forehead, a fine straight nose with a narrow bridge, almond-shaped brown eyes under gently arched light-brown brows, lids lowered in a recollected gaze, softly rounded cheeks, a small rosy mouth, a small rounded chin; light-brown hair parted in the centre under a white inner veil and a blue mantle drawn over the head. The Christ Child as in recurring-figures.md: a plump, ROUND baby face with full rosy cheeks, a high rounded forehead, a small button nose, large clear brown eyes, a small rosy mouth, soft short golden-brown curls, a plain gold halo, about forty days old, eyes open, one small hand reaching up to Simeon's beard. St. Joseph as in recurring-figures.md: a man of about forty with a LONG OVAL face — a straight nose, gentle dark-brown eyes under level brows, a quiet mouth; full dark-brown curly hair to the nape and a short full dark-brown beard; green tunic and ochre-brown mantle. Simeon: a very old man of about eighty-five with a LONG, NARROW face — a high, lined forehead, a slightly hooked nose, deep-set eyes wet with joy under white brows, hollow cheeks over high cheekbones; a long, soft white beard that divides into two locks, and white hair falling to the shoulders, uncovered. Anna: a woman of about eighty-four with a small, HEART-SHAPED face tapering to a pointed chin — a fine thin nose, bright dark eyes deep in soft wrinkles, a small smiling mouth; grey hair hidden under her dark veil.
cards.basis: Luke 2:22-38 gives the scene: the offering of two turtledoves, Simeon taking the Child in his arms, and Anna the prophetess of eighty-four. Tradition paints Simeon as a very old man with a long white beard and Anna in a dark veil; Our Lady, the Child and Joseph keep their faces from recurring-figures.md. The card also serves the fourth Joyful Mystery.

cards.subject: A procession of relics in the Romanesque nave of the Basilica of St. Servatius in Maastricht, as in its Heiligdomsvaart: at the centre, carried shoulder-high on poles under a gold-fringed canopy by four bearers in white surplices over dark cassocks, the great gilded house-shaped reliquary chest of St. Servatius (the Noodkist), with little gilded figures of apostles under arches, enamel bands and rock crystals shining; before it a server swings a smoking censer and two servers carry tall lit candles; behind, a priest in a gold cope walks with joined hands. Round Romanesque arches, pale stone columns and candlelight fill the background. Figures small to half-length and serene, the shrine the focus. No lettering. Keep the procession inside the arched window.
cards.face: The bearers and servers are secondary and differ: the front bearer, about thirty, with a long face and short dark hair in profile; the bearer beside him, about fifty, with a broad ruddy face and grey temples; a fair, round-faced boy server of about twelve with the censer; the priest in the gold cope, about sixty-five, clean-shaven with a lean, narrow face and white hair, eyes lowered.
cards.basis: The Pictorial Lives explains the feast by the Council of Trent's teaching that the bodies of the saints are to be honoured. The card paints that honour in a real rite: the relics procession of Maastricht, where the reliquary chest of St. Servatius, the Noodkist, is carried in procession (photographed under its canopy in 1962) and then set on the choir steps.
